The '''1971 New Zealand National Soccer League''' was the second season of a nationwide [[Round-robin tournament|round-robin]] club competition in [[New Zealand]] football. The league was expanded at the end of the inaugural season, so there was no relegation from the 1970 league season. [[Hungaria (soccer)|Hungaria]], who had competed in the inaugural season, combined with [[Miramar Rangers]] to form a new composite league team, [[Wellington City (soccer)|Wellington City]]. Though Miramar withdrew from the team after the 1971 season, the team continued to use the new name.<ref name="Hilton856">Hilton (1991), pp. 85-86</ref>

==Promotion to the national league==
At the end of the 1970 season, the winners of the Northern, Central, and Southern leagues — [[Mount Albert-Ponsonby]] (Auckland), [[Waterside (soccer)|Waterside]] (Wellington), and [[Caversham (soccer)|Caversham]] (Dunedin) respectively — took part in a play-off series to decide the two teams which would be granted entry to the national league. the results were as follows:

As a result of these matches, [[Mount Albert-Ponsonby]] and [[Caversham (soccer)|Caversham]] gained entry to the national league. In order to mount a stronger southern challenge, Caversham amalgamated with several other Dunedin-based sides to form [[Dunedin Suburbs]]; the team lasted for one season in this form before reverting to Caversham.<ref>{{cite web |title=New Zealand 1970 |url=https://www.rsssf.org/tablesn/nz70.html |website=[[RSSSF]] |access-date=13 April 2021}}</ref>

==Team performance==
The same four teams dominated the league as in the inaugural season, but this time it was [[Eastern Suburbs (soccer)|Eastern Suburbs]] who finished on top. An unbeaten run of twelve matches by [[Mount Wellington (soccer)|Mount Wellington]] saw them move into second place, followed by [[Christchurch United]] and [[Blockhouse Bay (soccer)|Blockhouse Bay]]. The league title came down to the last round of matches and a controversial yet thrilling between the top two sides. In front of an estimated crowd of 10,000 at Newmarket Park, the Mount had three goals disallowed yet still managed to draw against Suburbs 2-2. Despite still having one game in hand, the Mount needed a win to hang onto its title chances, and Suburbs were crowned champions. A personal milestone occurred for Eastern Suburbs' [[John Wrathall (footballer)|John Wrathall]], who scored his 1000th goal in 26 years of senior football during Suburbs' 3–1 win against [[Mount Albert-Ponsonby]].<ref name="Hilton856"/>

The gap between the top four and the rest closed considerably over the debut season for [[Gisborne City]], who finished comfortably fifth. below that was a major gap, however, with [[Dunedin Suburbs (soccer)|Dunedin Suburbs]], [[Mount Albert-Ponsonby]], [[Stop Out]], [[Wellington City (soccer)|Wellington City]], and [[Western Suburbs FC (New Zealand)|Western Suburbs FC]] all battling to avoid relegation. Wellington's teams struggled in the league for a second season, filling all three bottom places, and it was Porirua-based Western Suburbs which finished last on goal average. If goal difference had been employed — a system which was to be introduced for the [[1978 New Zealand National Soccer League|1978 league]] — they would have survived and it would have been City who went down.<ref name="Hilton856"/>
